title: Connections: Atlas
desc: Find the geographical thread linking each set

questions.q: What connects: Iceland, Madagascar, Cuba, and Sri Lanka?
questions.a: They're all island nations that are also the largest island in their respective regions — and none of them touch a continental mainland

questions.q: Odd one out: Amazon, Nile, Yangtze, Danube. Which and why?
questions.a: Danube — it's the only one that flows through more than 4 countries (10 countries). Also the shortest. But the intended answer: it's the only one entirely in Europe

questions.q: What connects: Chile, Norway, New Zealand, and Japan?
questions.a: They're all long, narrow countries running roughly north-south, with mountainous spines and significant coastlines

questions.q: Put these deserts in order of size, smallest to largest: Gobi, Sahara, Arabian, Kalahari
questions.a: Kalahari (900k km²) → Arabian (2.3M km²) → Gobi (1.3M km²)... actually: Kalahari → Gobi → Arabian → Sahara (9.2M km²)

questions.q: What connects: The Strait of Gibraltar, the Bosphorus, and the Strait of Malacca?
questions.a: They're all narrow waterways connecting two larger bodies of water AND separating two landmasses — and all are strategically vital chokepoints for global shipping

questions.q: What connects: Timbuktu, El Dorado, and Shangri-La?
questions.a: All are 'legendary' places — Timbuktu is real (in Mali) but became a byword for remoteness; El Dorado and Shangri-La are fictional but inspired real expeditions

questions.q: True, false, or it depends: 'Africa is a country'
questions.a: False — Africa is a continent with 54 recognised countries. This is worth saying because surveys show a troubling number of people genuinely believe it's one country

questions.q: What connects: Mount Kilimanjaro, Mount Elbrus, and Denali?
questions.a: They're each the highest peak on their respective continent — Africa, Europe, and North America

questions.q: Two of these capitals are on the 'wrong' side of their country (e.g. not centrally located). Which? Washington DC, Canberra, Brasília, Ottawa
questions.a: Washington DC and Ottawa — both are on the eastern edge. Canberra and Brasília were specifically built to be more central

questions.q: What connects: Panama hats, Turkish baths, and Chinese checkers?
questions.a: None of them come from the place in their name — Panama hats are from Ecuador, Turkish baths originated in Rome, and Chinese checkers were invented in Germany
